subject: Realtime response lag impacting streaming chat (Novus.ai) - action owners and short-term mitigations
messages:
From: Elena Costa <elena@novus.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: High token latency in streaming chat - affecting live customer flows

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We started seeing large delays in token emission for our live chat sessions at ~09:05 UTC this morning. For multiple users the stream stalls for 2-4 seconds between tokens and sometimes times out entirely requiring a retry. This is impacting our checkout support flow (customers abandon).

Quick details:
- Region: us-east1
- Model: redwood-v2-stream-7B (default streaming endpoint)
- Example session id: novus-sess-9f3b6 (we're attaching traces)
- First observed: 09:05 UTC, steady since then with spikes every ~15-20 minutes

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side and what mitigation steps we should take immediately? We need short-term workarounds while you investigate root cause.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Costa
Head of Platform
Novus.ai

Attachment: streaming_trace_request.txt (text)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Costa <elena@novus.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High token latency in streaming chat - immediate steps

Hi Elena - thanks for the heads up and the session id. We’re seeing elevated tail latencies on the streaming emitter in us-east1 that align with your timestamps. Engineering is paged.

Short-term mitigations you can apply immediately (minimal code change):
1) If you can tolerate non-streaming for critical flows, set streaming=false on the conversation endpoint; this will return a single response and avoid token-by-token emission delays.
2) Reduce max_tokens and max_response_time for the high-throughput checkout flows to limit per-request compute. We suggest max_tokens=256 for now.
3) Add client-side exponential backoff for streaming reads (250ms -> 500ms -> 1s) and retry once if stream stalls for >3s.
4) If you have dedicated capacity or can route to a smaller model variant (redwood-v2-chat-3B), temporarily switch routing to that model to preserve throughput.

We’ve requested traces from our runtime and will push a short-term mitigation (priority config change) to reduce batching heuristics that appear to be causing kernel scheduling contention. I’ve attached a lightweight trace request (streaming_trace_request.txt) — if you can forward any server-side logs or a raw websocket trace for novus-sess-9f3b6 that would help.

I’ll update you within 60 minutes with the engineering action. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your live customers.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High token latency in streaming chat - quick coordination (internal)

Karthik / Rishi — routing this to you both. Engineering note: initial traces show the emitter batch window increasing under mixed small/big prompt workloads which pushes kernel selection into a higher-latency path when sequence lengths vary. Short-term we can:
- Flip the emitter batch-size ceiling to 8 for us-east1 pool for 30 minutes to reduce inter-request waiting.
- Force model variant fallback for customers flagged as "checkout-critical" (Novus is flagged).
- Disable optimistic KV-cache prefetch for the affected infra slice while we stabilize kernel scheduling.

Karthik: can you push the batch-size ceiling flip and rollback plan? Communicate ETA here so Rishi can pass to Novus.

Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Costa <elena@novus.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High token latency in streaming chat - mitigation applied and recommended config

Elena,

Update: we applied a temporary batch-size ceiling reduction and disabled the KV-cache prefetch for the affected us-east1 slice at 10:42 UTC. You should see token emission return to normal for most sessions.

What we changed and what you should do client-side:
- Server: batch-size ceiling -> 8 for 30 minutes; KV-cache prefetch disabled; fallback routing enabled to redwood-v2-chat-3B for flagged accounts.
- Client: for highest-traffic checkout paths, switch to streaming=false or route to redwood-v2-chat-3B until we confirm stability.
- If you keep streaming=true, implement the recommended backoff and a single automatic retry when a stall exceeds 3s.

I’ve attached our streaming mitigation runbook (redwood_streaming_runbook_v1.pdf) with quick CLI commands and the ticket tracking link. We’re still investigating root cause (kernel scheduling + mixed-sequence batching) and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

Can you confirm whether you’re seeing improvement and if you want us to flip your routing to the 3B variant automatically? If you’d like, we can schedule a short 15-min bridge to walk through the temporary flags.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_streaming_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Costa <elena@novus.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@novus.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High token latency in streaming chat - mitigation applied and recommended config

Thanks Rishi — we’re seeing much better behavior after your change (latency back to normal for ~95% of sessions). We flipped the critical checkout path to streaming=false and added the backoff to the client. Few follow-ups:

- Can you share the ETA for the full rollback to normal batch heuristics?
- We’ll file a billing review for possible usage credits given the impact; what’s the best contact?
- Please include a short postmortem when available that covers root cause and long-term remediation.

Appreciate the quick response and runbook. If helpful, we can join a short bridge tomorrow to review traces.

Elena
Elena Costa
Head of Platform, Novus.ai
